entities.summary:
The COVID-19 pandemic in Bhutan was a public health crisis that occurred in 2020, affecting the country of Bhutan. 

 The pandemic, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, was first reported in Bhutan on March 6, 2020, and spread rapidly throughout the country. 

 The government of Bhutan implemented various measures to contain the spread of the virus, including lockdowns, travel restrictions, and quarantines. 

 Despite these efforts, the pandemic had a significant impact on the country, causing widespread disruption to daily life, economic hardship, and a significant increase in the number of cases and deaths. 

 In the end, the pandemic was brought under control, but not before it had a lasting impact on the country and its people.

 The COVID-19 pandemic in Bhutan was a stark reminder of the fragility of human life and the importance of preparedness and resilience in the face of global health crises.
